# Can a Small Language Model Do Physics Without a Tool Call?

## A TinyLLM Router and a Fixed Physics Engine in One Graph

A car does 30 m/s on a wet road and brakes hard. How far does it travel before stopping? An LLM answers from what it has seen; a calculator answers from the equations. The two don't always agree.

The usual fix is a tool call: the model writes the sum and Python does it. [Qwenputer](https://huggingface.co/divagr1925/Qwen3.5-4B-Qwenputer) takes the other route and puts a CPU inside the weights of Qwen3.5-4B. This post tries the same idea at a much smaller scale. Newton net is a tiny language model (about 0.25–0.5M parameters) that reads a short driving question, picks one of the equations of motion, and runs that equation in a fixed physics engine inside its own forward pass. The engine's maths is exact and frozen; the language model is trained through it, so a wrong route or a misread variable from input text costs a wrong answer. It is tested on 800 held-out questions for route accuracy, answer error and how often it correctly refuses questions it can't answer.
